_comment: §4 condition 3 of api-growth-method.md, as a machine-checkable ledger.
The campaign may not terminate with categories unexercised. That condition is
the one the method ORIGINALLY MISSED: its first draft terminated on 'contract
green, blind run clean, remaining leaks not owned', all of which Outlander
alone can satisfy. An API proven against one consumer is an API shaped like
⚠ `proven` means a TEST that runs, named in `proof`. Not a plan, not a doc
paragraph, not 'it would obviously work'. Rule 2 of the campaign: name a test,
never a doc marker. Prose-asserted claims have gone red on prose three times
⚠ Do not mark a row proven because the code exists somewhere. The question is
whether the CATEGORY exercised the public API — Sanic existing in-tree is not
the same fact as Sanic standing up through `ambition::app` standalone AND
The ORDER these are attacked stays evidence-driven (§3 selects each slice from
what the previous one measured). The CATEGORIES are not optional.

categories.proof: fixtures/external_consumer/tests/composition.rs — one mounted module reaches both faces; gameplay.rs drives a real session

categories.proves: optional-capability closure — does a small game link menus, persistence, audio, bosses?
categories.proof: fixtures/minimal_game/tests/boots.rs — 7 tests: one module boots BOTH faces, reaches a RUNNING host via `ambition::app::host_status`, and a game that can never start REFUSES promptly and names the cause. Ratcheted by `minimal-game-names-only-the-public-sdk`, baseline ZERO.
categories.note: The blind run showed a minimal module cannot even reach the windowed face: it panics without a CharacterCatalog. This category is what turns §2e's '41 ambition crates from 2 declared dependencies' from a number into a felt constraint or a non-issue. RESULT: it names 4 modules to Outlander's 14, and all four are one hole — PlatformerExperienceAuthoring + PreparedPlatformerSource + RoomSpec + engine_core geometry. A minimal game can COMPOSE through the SDK and still cannot DECLARE a room or an experience through it.
categories.answers_optional_capability_closure: PARTLY, and the partly is the finding. A movement-only game links and must DECLARE audio it does not have — preparation validation refuses an experience with no audio fragment, so silence is mandatory paperwork. It needs no menus, persistence, LDtk or bosses of its own, and no `bevy` dependency at all. Five modules total: four are the room/experience declaration path, the fifth is the silent audio fragment.
categories.ratchet: ZERO — names only ambition::app, ambition::world, and the documented bevy re-export

categories.proof: fixtures/minimal_game/tests/boots.rs — `a_noncombat_character_gets_no_combat_state`: the live body of a RUNNING host carries 60+ components and not one is melee, combat, hitbox, health or moveset state. Non-vacuity asserted first.
categories.correction: ⚠ FIRST RECORDED AS FAILING, 2026-07-30, and that was MY error. The first attempt asserted `AbilityBase.attack == false` and failed. But the ability mask is not armament: `actor_clusters.rs` states that a combat body HAS the attack verb as a capability, while whether it SWINGS is gated by `ActionSet.melee` and the brain — a peaceful NPC folds no `attack` move and carries no `MovesetMelee`. Asking about components instead of the mask answers the row's actual question, and the answer is that the design is correct. The wrong version is left visible in the test's doc comment: a campaign that only records the findings it got right is a campaign nobody can calibrate against.

categories.proves: reusable module + namespace identity; the SAME content and schema fingerprints both ways
categories.note: Both halves required. Standalone alone proves nothing about identity.
categories.measured: HALF the claim holds, and the half that does not is a DESIGN GAP rather than a bug. ADR 0032 says module inclusion is 'a MERGE, not an ordering... with transactional conflict detection'. The conflict detection is real and now tested: two modules both declaring an experience are refused, and the error names both claimants and both values (`two_modules_declaring_an_experience_conflict_and_the_error_names_both`). But a composition holds exactly ONE experience, so mounting two real games side by side is not expressible at all — the second module's `experience()` COLLIDES rather than being namespaced under the composition.
categories.what_would_prove_it: An in-tree module (Sanic or Mary-O) mounts through `PlatformerApp` standalone AND alongside another module, with content and rollback-schema identities compared across the two compositions by a TEST. The second half is blocked on module-qualified namespaces, which ADR 0032 defers.
categories.blocked_on: module-qualified namespaces. ⚠ This is the evidence that the deferral has a COST and what the cost is — which is what the deferral was waiting for. A namespace scheme designed before the collision would have been a guess; the collision now exists and is reproducible.

standalone_half.proof: game/ambition_demo_sanic/tests/stands_up_through_the_sdk.rs — Sanic mounts through `PlatformerApp` and reaches a RUNNING host (not merely composes), on the first attempt with NO engine changes.
standalone_half.why_it_matters: Sanic PREDATES the SDK. Outlander and the minimal game were written or rewritten against `ambition::app`; Sanic was not, and it carries presentation profiles, a declared HUD, music, procedural SFX and packed SFX. It is the closest thing to an independent consumer available, which is what §4's carve decision needs — a footprint measured only against games the API author designed answers a weaker question.
standalone_half.what_it_says_about_playable: Sanic mounts as a `capability`, not through `playable()`, because `playable` carries no presentation profiles or HUD declaration. That is recorded as evidence about where `playable` stops rather than patched by inventing parameters from one caller.

categories.no_ratchet_note: ⚠ Sanic gets NO allowlist ratchet, deliberately. The allowlist is scoped to `fixtures/` (Jon, 2026-07-30); extending it to `game/` would answer the deferred `ambition_content`-depends-on-the-facade question by accident, in a row about something else. In-tree consumers are measured when that question is actually taken.

categories.proves: participants, character selection, atomic match lifecycle, scoped rules, rollback
categories.note: Rollback as a public knob is deferred to its own slice; this category depends on that.
Deliberately last. It is also the consumer whose facade dependency ADR 0031 records as a deferred MEASUREMENT question rather than a rule.
